Tenerife.authority: Cabildo de Tenerife (island-wide portal, 12 trees, JS-rendered, licence not yet checked) PLUS a genuine new find: Ayuntamiento de Santa Cruz de Tenerife open data portal, dataset 'arboles-singulares'
Tenerife.url: https://www.santacruzdetenerife.es/opendata/dataset/7850581f-371b-4307-a635-3a8c2802a964/resource/4e82859e-052c-4de2-a70a-abff7be9e297/download/arboles_singulares.json (also .csv, .xls, .kml siblings); Cabildo portal: custodiadelterritorio-style JS site, url not re-fetched this pass, see BRIEF's own Tenerife note
Tenerife.licence: CC BY, proven: the dataset page (https://www.santacruzdetenerife.es/opendata/dataset/arboles-singulares) links http://www.opendefinition.org/licenses/cc-by under class='...license'. This is a genuine open-data licence, verified by fetching the dataset page directly (HTTP 200).
Tenerife.fields: NOM_COMUN, GENERO, ESPECIE, FAMILIA, ORIGEN, GEOCODIGO, coordinates (GeoJSON Point, WGS84, tree-level), UTM_X/UTM_Y. No age field, no girth field, no vitality field, no access field. ENLACE field for a per-tree detail page says 'coming soon, in process' for every entry checked, so no richer per-tree page exists yet.
Tenerife.count: 63 designated singular trees, all within the municipality of Santa Cruz de Tenerife (the island's capital, not the whole island). This is IN ADDITION to the Cabildo's island-wide 12, which the existing Tenerife page (4 trees) already draws from.
Tenerife.note: This is a genuine new register the existing OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md and passcheck do not know about: a municipal 'arboles singulares' open-data catalogue for the capital, semantically filtered (designated singular trees, not a bulk street-tree inventory) and CC BY licensed, confirmed by fetching the licence page directly rather than trusting a search summary. What is missing before it can ship as a register file: age, girth and vitality are all absent, so every candidate still needs the normal two-source verify pass and a species/age lookup elsewhere (iNaturalist, the future 'ficha' pages once published, or WebSearch per tree). Species names in this file are Spanish common names and Latin binomials split across GENERO+ESPECIE (needs joining, e.g. 'Acacia' + 'nilotica'). Next step for a build pass: python3-import this JSON into data/registers/tenerife-santacruz-arboles-singulares.json with a licence block, then cluster_register.py it against the existing 4 Tenerife trees to see what's walkable from the capital. The Cabildo's separate island-wide 12-tree JS portal (source of the existing Drago Milenario / Vilaflor pines entries) was not re-scouted this pass since the brief already established it as a lead list without a proven licence; treat it as unscouted-for-licence rather than re-verified.

Gran Canaria.authority: Cabildo de Gran Canaria, Catalogo Insular de Arboles Singulares (Decreto 15 November 2021), plus a separate municipal catalogue for the capital: Ayuntamiento de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
Gran Canaria.url: https://custodiadelterritorio.grancanaria.com/en/arboles-singulares (insular, per-tree 'ficha' pages on a Liferay CMS); https://lpgcsostenible.laspalmasgc.es/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Catalogo_arboles_LPGC.pdf (municipal, 326 specimens across 181 fichas)
Gran Canaria.licence: NOT PROVEN for either source. The insular custodiadelterritorio.grancanaria.com page fetched clean (HTTP 200, 320KB) but is a per-tree CMS page with no licence statement found in the fetched HTML head or footer. The municipal PDF sits on lpgcsostenible.laspalmasgc.es, whose /aviso-legal returned a 301 redirect this pass did not follow (time-boxed); no licence sentence quotable yet from either. Until one is fetched and quoted, both stay ungated for import despite good data.
Gran Canaria.fields: Insular catalogue (per news coverage, not yet fetched from a per-tree ficha this pass): age (explicitly, up to 400 years for the oldest, e.g. the acebuche of Llano Parra and the sabina of Tirma), a visitability/access flag (11 of the insular 77-85 are recorded as not accessible to visitors, which is exactly the field hard rule 10 needs), species, dimensions. Municipal PDF: not opened this pass, format and fields unconfirmed beyond '326 specimens, 181 fichas' from press coverage.
Gran Canaria.count: Insular: sources disagree, 77 or 85 selected from a field survey of 273 candidates (both figures appear in different press pieces, so treat as approximate until the primary source is read). Municipal (Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, the capital): 326 specimens across 181 fichas, covering the whole city, so likely several within any walkable cluster of the capital.
Gran Canaria.note: Genuinely promising: this is the first Canary source in this pass with an AGE field and an explicit access/visitability flag, which is rarer than most mainland Spanish regional registers this project has imported. What is in the way is purely licence proof and structured data extraction, not a designation question. Next steps for whoever picks this up: (1) fetch https://lpgcsostenible.laspalmasgc.es/aviso-legal with -L to follow the redirect and quote its reuse terms, or find a dedicated Cabildo/Ayuntamiento open-data portal (datos.grancanaria.com or similar, searched for but not found this pass); (2) if no open licence exists, the per-tree custodiadelterritorio fichas may still be usable as a verification source under the same rules as monumentaltrees.com, i.e. one browser-viewed page at a time, never bulk. Also worth noting for whoever verifies: the insular catalogue's own legal basis is unsettled (a legal report found the Cabildo lacks competence to enforce the ordinance pending a regional biodiversity law), which affects protection status, not whether the trees themselves are real, old or worth a visit.

La Palma.note: Searched for a Cabildo de La Palma singular-tree catalogue analogous to Tenerife and Gran Canaria's; found none. Search results returned only Gran Canaria coverage and a 2019 press line noting that historically 'only Tenerife has an insular catalogue of trees and singular groves besides Gran Canaria', implying La Palma had none as of that date. Properly scouted for this pass (two targeted searches, no promising lead surfaced); route for a future city pass is the cheap non-register path: local press ('la palma arbol mas viejo/singular'), the Caldera de Taburiente national park's own visitor materials, and monumentaltrees.com as a cross-check, one tree at a time.

La Gomera.authority: none found as a formal catalogue; the island's known trees are the Drago Milenario-adjacent Garajonay laurisilva forest and named individual dragon trees such as the Drago de Agalan
La Gomera.note: No Cabildo de La Gomera singular-tree register surfaced. What did surface is press coverage of the Drago de Agalan (over 400 years old per multiple local press pieces, the oldest and largest dragon tree on La Gomera) and the Garajonay National Park laurisilva itself (UNESCO World Heritage, over 10% of the island). Garajonay is a protected forest, not a collectible point under this project's own rule (an avenue or a whole wood is blocked), so any entry from here would be individual named trees like the Drago de Agalan, verified the ordinary two-source way, not a register import. Route for a future pass: local press plus the national park's own published visitor/species materials (parquesnacionales.es), same cheap non-register path as La Palma.

Madeira.authority: Instituto das Florestas e Conservacao da Natureza (IFCN Madeira), VALCONMAC/ASMAC survey 'Arvores e bosques singulares da Madeira e Porto Santo'
Madeira.url: ifcn.madeira.gov.pt/images/FotosArtigos/Florestas/ASMAC/ASMACnn.pdf (numbered PDF cards; the exact nn range a previous pass walked, 71-100, is not fully reproducible: this pass spot-checked ASMAC85.pdf and got a 404, so the working numbers need re-walking rather than assumed)
Madeira.licence: NOT PROVEN. This pass fetched ifcn.madeira.gov.pt's homepage directly (HTTP 200 after a 301 to /pt/, 909KB) and searched it for any data-reuse licence statement (Creative Commons, 'dados abertos', 'reutilizacao'). None found; every 'licenca' hit on the page is a hunting or fishing permit, unrelated to data reuse. Portuguese public bodies often allow free reuse of official documents by default, but that is not the same as a quotable licence sentence, and this register-layer's own rule treats the absence of one as a hard gate regardless of how good the data is.
Madeira.fields: Per OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md 2026-08-17 (a prior pass, not re-verified here): species, height, maximum perimeter/perimeters, a rough age note, WGS84 coordinates, and an access-and-ownership field. That access field is unusually good: it already blocked 4 of 12 entries for this project (a private hotel garden, a children's care institution, a private rural hotel).
Madeira.count: 11 Madeira entries plus 1 on Porto Santo, per the prior pass; not recounted this pass since the PDF numbering did not reproduce cleanly on the one spot-check tried.
Madeira.note: This island was flagged in the brief as already scouted by a same-day commit (b36f949, OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md), and that write-up is thorough on content but records no licence proof, which this pass tried and failed to supply. Two things for whoever picks this up next: (1) find the actual working PDF numbers again (71-100 did not hold at 85 this pass, HTTP 404) by browsing the ASMAC listing page on ifcn.madeira.gov.pt rather than guessing numbers cold; (2) look specifically for a Portuguese open-data portal covering the autonomous region (dados.gov.pt sometimes carries regional bodies, or IFCN may have its own 'dados abertos' section not linked from the homepage) since that is where a quotable CC-style licence is most likely to live, rather than a plain institutional PDF page. Until a licence sentence is found, this register-layer import stays gated even though the underlying data is exactly what this project wants (age note plus access field together).

Azores.authority: Direção Regional dos Recursos Florestais e Ordenamento Territorial (DRRF), Secretaria Regional da Agricultura e Alimentação, drrf.azores.gov.pt; confirmed that the Azores keep their own forestry administration separate from the mainland
Azores.url: https://drrf.azores.gov.pt/ and https://drrf.azores.gov.pt/areas-de-atuacao/ found and not yet fetched directly this pass
Azores.note: Confirmed precondition first, per the brief: portugal-icnf.json's own scope field states it is 'the complete national register, all 18 mainland districts' with zero entries matching 'acor'/'azor' anywhere in the 555 rows, so the Azores are genuinely uncovered by what we already hold. One search for a monumental/classified-tree register under DRRF surfaced the department itself but no register page or dataset; a second, more targeted search (the Portuguese legal term 'arvore de interesse publico', which is how mainland Portugal's AIP designation is named, applied to Acores) was not run this pass, out of time. That specific search is the right next step before concluding empty: Portugal's AIP classification is a national legal category and the Azores may run their own parallel list under it the way Madeira runs ASMAC outside ICNF. Left honestly unscouted rather than guessed at.

Corsica.authority: Office de l'Environnement de la Corse (OEC) with the Conservatoire botanique national de Corse, programme name 'L'arburi nutevuli' / 'Arbres remarquables de Corse', running since 2004
Corsica.url: https://www.oec.corsica/L-arburi-nutevuli_a19.html (fetched directly, HTTP 200, 96KB); a Facebook page 'Arbres Remarquables de Corse' and a photo gallery at oec.corsica/photos also exist per search but were not fetched
Corsica.licence: not found. The fetched page is almost entirely navigation/menu markup; no licence, CC or data-reuse statement was found in it. Three linked PDFs on the page (Fiche_INV_2013.pdf, Fiche_INV_peuplements_2013.pdf, Fiche_INV_Notice_2013.pdf, all on the old oec.fr domain) read as SUBMISSION forms for nominating a tree to the inventory, not the inventory's own output, so they are not a data source even before a licence question.
Corsica.fields: not confirmed from the primary source. A WebSearch summary (a lead, not evidence per this project's own rule on search summaries) described roughly 200 'vegetation monuments' selected by a technical commission meeting twice a year, as of December 2023, but this pass could not locate the actual list, map or dataset behind that number on oec.corsica itself; the fetched page's real body text did not surface in a quick extraction (mostly jQuery menu code), so a longer read of the same page, or its photo gallery and Facebook page, is the honest next step.
Corsica.count: unconfirmed, roughly 200 per an unverified search summary, not seen on the primary source
Corsica.note: This is a real, active, government-linked programme, not a dead end, so it earns 'stalled' rather than 'empty'. What is in the way is purely navigation: the page found is a landing page describing the programme and how to submit a nomination, not the register output itself. Next step: look for a Corsica open-data portal (the Collectivité de Corse may run one separately from OEC) or ask the OEC site for a public map/liste rather than the landing page, and read the fetched HTML's actual article body (article id 9582608 in the page's own JS) rather than the menu chrome that dominated this pass's quick extraction.

Sardinia.authority: Regione Sardegna, Corpo Forestale e di Vigilanza Ambientale (CFVA) and the FoReSTAS agency, publishing through Sardegna Geoportale; explicitly tied to the national 'Elenco degli Alberi Monumentali d'Italia' under Legge 10/2013 and the decree of 23/10/2014, the same legal framework Sicily's register turned out to republish verbatim
Sardinia.url: http://www.sardegnageoportale.it/index.php?xsl=2425&s=377329&v=2&c=14469&t=1&tb=14401 (fetched, HTTP 200, 17KB); also https://www.sardegnaambiente.it (CFVA activity pages) and it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberi_monumentali_della_Sardegna
Sardinia.licence: not found this pass. The geoportale page fetched clean but no CC/IODL/open-data licence phrase was found in its 17KB (a thin page, likely mostly a viewer shell rather than the data itself). Sardegna Geoportale elsewhere in this project's experience often publishes under IODL (Italian Open Data Licence), but that has not been quoted from this specific page yet.
Sardinia.fields: unconfirmed from the primary source this pass; search results describe it as 'a geographic layer containing the points corresponding to the monumental trees censused... included in the List of Monumental Trees of Italy', which is the same framing Sicily's register used before turning out to be a same-data republish with no age or vitality field.
Sardinia.count: 431 trees regionwide per an October 2025 update (search summary, not yet primary-source verified), described as the Italian region with the most monumental trees, concentrated in the Barbagia/Ogliastra sub-region rather than near the main coastal towns; our existing italy-masaf.json already holds 4 entries near the island per the brief.
Sardinia.note: Genuinely undecided, and it matters more than Sicily's answer did because Sardinia is a bigger island with more entries. Sicily's precedent (same sheet ids, same decree, no age/vitality, not an independent second source) is the way to bet, but Piemonte and Puglia are the counter-precedent: both are Italian regions this project already imports as SEPARATE, richer register files (piemonte-alberi-monumentali.json, puglia-alberi-monumentali.json) alongside italy-masaf.json, so 'regional geoportal republishing MASAF' is not automatically a dead end for Italian regions in general. This pass ran out of time before opening the geoportal layer's actual attribute table (the fetched page is a viewer/search shell, not raw data) to settle which case Sardinia is. Next step, ten minutes: open the geoportale's underlying WFS/download link (usually a 'scarica dati' or API link off this same page) and check for an age or vitality column before concluding either way; do not re-fetch the landing page, go straight for the data endpoint.
